title: The Witness of the Marlowe Estate
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Marlowe is exhumed for a heritage ceremony and found empty, concierge Hazel Joubert—whose hotel has hosted every secret in Marlowe's Crossing for thirty years—is the only person who remembers a second funeral, held quietly at midnight forty years ago. Pulled into an investigation by the founder's guilt-ridden granddaughter, Hazel traces the empty coffin to a witness who testified against the Marlowe family and was declared dead, only to be hidden away by the very constable sworn to bury the truth. As the anniversary dinner approaches and someone begins silencing the old guard one by one, Hazel must choose between protecting her found family at the hotel and exposing a justice that was never legal but may have been right. In the end, she finds the witness alive, forces the town to hear the truth at the anniversary toast, and accepts that being seen is the price of belonging.
about_author: Odile Lockridge is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent a decade collecting the confessions of traveling strangers. She writes mysteries about people who see everything and are seen by no one.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Hazel Joubert, concierge of the Bellamy Hotel, watches the exhumation of town founder Edmund Marlowe from the lobby window—and recognizes the undertaker's face from a midnight burial decades ago. When the coffin is opened and empty, her carefully maintained invisibility cracks. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in professional composure.

chapters.title: A Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Marlowe's granddaughter Vivian arrives at the hotel demanding answers, and Hazel realizes the girl is asking questions Hazel herself buried years ago. Flashback threads reveal the 1984 inquest that ruled a factory fire an accident despite a witness's testimony. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming over shared suspicion.

chapters.title: The Register of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Hazel mines thirty years of guest registers, receipts, and overheard conversations, mapping who lied about their whereabouts the week of the fire. The old constable, Aldous Pike, warns her off with unsettling gentleness. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by fear of what she's finding.

chapters.title: What the Night Porter Knew
chapters.summary: Hazel tracks down retired night porter Edda Solano, who confesses she drove a terrified young woman—a witness named Ruth—to the train station the night after the fire, and never saw her again. That same evening, Edda's cottage is ransacked. POV: alternating Hazel and Edda. Emotional beat: grief for complicity, urgency rising.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: The town prepares its centennial dinner while Hazel discovers the anniversary committee's minutes were altered to erase Ruth's family name entirely. Vivian confronts her own father, councilman Gerald Marlowe, and is coldly rebuffed. POV: Vivian. Emotional beat: love against duty as family loyalty fractures.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Wine Cellar
chapters.summary: Following a ledger discrepancy, Hazel finds evidence that Pike falsified the death certificate—but also letters suggesting he did it to protect Ruth from the Marlowes' hired men, not to bury her. The line between villain and guardian blurs. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; justice outside the law cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Someone at the Desk
chapters.summary: A quiet elderly guest checks in under a false name, tips too generously, and flinches at the sound of the grandfather clock. Hazel notices everything—and realizes the woman signs her register with a tremor matching the handwriting on Ruth's old testimony. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: breathless recognition, tenderness toward a frightened stranger.

chapters.title: The Clock Strikes Wrong
chapters.summary: Gerald Marlowe learns the witness lives and sends men to the hotel; Hazel hides Ruth in the wine cellar while the staff—her ragtag found family—run interference during a packed pre-anniversary reception. Pike arrives and stands between them. POV: ensemble, anchored by Hazel. Emotional beat: terror transformed into fierce solidarity.

chapters.title: A Toast to the Founder
chapters.summary: At the centennial dinner, Hazel and Vivian hijack the toast: Ruth appears before three hundred guests and tells what she saw the night of the fire. Gerald's counterattack collapses when Pike produces the forged certificate and his own confession. POV: Ruth, then Hazel. Emotional beat: catharsis—the silenced voice finally heard.

chapters.title: The Visible Woman
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the town reckons with its founding myth; Ruth stays on as the hotel's historian, Pike faces trial on his own terms, and Hazel—who once prided herself on closing cases invisibly—accepts the front-page byline and a place in the community she served unseen. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
